title: Oh, What a Struggle Wakes Within
description: Oh, What a Struggle Wakes Within in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 974 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Temptation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Oh, what a strug-gle wakes with-in, When in the spi-rit's so-li-tude, The tempt-ing, treach-erous thoughts of sin, In all their lur-ing smiles in-trude!

lines: Oh, what a struggle wakes within,
The tempting, treacherous thoughts of sin,
In all their luring smiles intrude!
'Tis then, my Father! then I feel
Like a poor trembling child I steal
To thee, for safety, and for rest.
Beneath thy shadow let me live!
Be thou my Friend — my Father be!
I bend in trust — I pray! forgive
The erring child that flies to thee!

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
